cards.front: Name two examples of cloud-based email/productivity suites.
cards.back: Microsoft 365 (Outlook in the cloud) and Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive).

cards.front: What are the key benefits of cloud-based productivity services over on-premises servers?
cards.back: Scalability (add resources on demand), redundancy (multiple connections and backups), anywhere access, and built-in backup and disaster recovery.

cards.front: How does cloud file synchronization (OneDrive/Google Drive) work?
cards.back: A local client monitors a designated folder. Files saved there are automatically uploaded and synced to the cloud, then mirrored to all other devices running the same client.

cards.front: What cloud feature allows multiple users to edit the same document simultaneously?
cards.back: Real-time co-editing (collaboration). Changes made by one user appear instantly for all other users viewing the same document.
Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), Okta, and Google Identity.

cards.front: What happens when an admin adds a user to a cloud identity system?
cards.back: The change is automatically propagated to all connected identity providers. No need to manually add the user in each system separately.

cards.front: What is the main advantage of cloud-based license management over traditional licensing?
cards.back: Centralized visibility and control. Admins can see all licenses, who is actively using them, and reassign unused licenses without buying new seats.
Microsoft's cloud-based identity provider (formerly Azure Active Directory). Manages user accounts and authentication for cloud services. Does not require an on-premises domain controller.
